name: Blue light acne device

lead: A blue light acne device is a handheld wand or mask that emits visible blue light, around 405 to 470 nanometers, onto acne-prone skin for a few minutes a day. Dermatology clinics use stronger versions, and consumer devices are lower power.
It is used as a drug-free adjunct for mild to moderate inflammatory acne.

paras: Cutibacterium acnes produces porphyrins that absorb blue light and generate reactive oxygen species, damaging the bacteria. The light may also have a mild anti-inflammatory effect on the skin.

Side effects are minor, such as temporary dryness or redness, and eye protection is advised. Meta-analyses find blue light can reduce lesions, but included trials are small, short and at risk of bias, so effectiveness versus standard treatments remains unclear. Combination blue and red light may do better in the short term, and home devices are weaker than clinic units.
